label: New beginnings
title: Bhagavad Gita for New Beginnings: 7 Verses to Start Well
description: Seven verses for a new job, city or chapter: action is how you begin (6.3), every start has flaws (18.48), and stand up and act (4.42). Sanskrit, plain English and one thing to try.
h1: Bhagavad Gita for new beginnings: 7 verses to start well
subtitle: For the new job, new city, new project or new chapter. Read one a day, or all seven before day one.
keywords: gita verses for a fresh start
intro: Krishna has advice for anyone at the start of something: for the one beginning, action is the way (6.3). These verses take you through a start. Every new thing comes with flaws, like fire with smoke (18.48). With steady effort it's within reach (6.36), so keep doing the work (3.19), cut through doubt (4.42) and step up (11.33). The last is from the Chhandogya Upanishad, a boy who walked off with four hundred thin cows and came back with a thousand.

image.altGlobal: A young woman carrying a plant into her new, empty apartment in morning light

days.heading: Beginners begin by doing
days.line: For one starting out on the path, action is the way. For one who has arrived, stillness is.
days.forYou: Krishna separates two stages. At the start, the way forward is action: showing up, practising, trying. Calm comes later, once you've arrived. A new beginning is a time to move.
days.today: Do one concrete thing for your new start today, before you plan anything else.

days.heading: Every start has smoke
days.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
days.forYou: Krishna's image is fire and smoke. Every new job, city or project will come with things that don't work. That's normal, and Krishna asks you to keep going when you hit them.
days.today: Write down the first thing that went wrong in your new start. Then write the next step anyway.
days.note: This answers perfectionism. If a place is harming you, leaving can be the right call.

days.heading: Within reach
days.line: Without self-control it's hard. With sincere effort and the right means, it's within reach.
days.forYou: Krishna is honest: this takes discipline. He's also clear that with sincere effort and the right method, it can be done. New things feel hard because they're new.
days.today: Pick one habit that will make your new start work, and do it daily for a week.

days.heading: Keep doing the work
days.line: So keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. That's how you rise.
days.forYou: After the excitement of the first day comes the long middle. Krishna's advice is plain: keep doing what needs doing, well, without obsessing over how it will turn out.
days.today: Do today's work as if it were your first day.

days.heading: Cut the doubt
days.line: Cut the doubt in your heart with clear understanding, then stand up and act.
days.forYou: Arjuna's doubts didn't go away on their own. Krishna tells him to cut them with understanding: get clear on what you know, then stand up. Doubt will visit any new start. You don't have to wait for it to leave.
days.today: Write your biggest doubt about this new start, and one fact that answers it.

days.heading: Step into your part
days.line: The story is already in motion. Rise and do your part; be the instrument.
days.forYou: Krishna tells Arjuna the larger story is already moving, and his job is to rise and play his part well. Starting something new means you've joined something bigger than you.
days.today: Introduce yourself to one person in your new place who will matter to your work.
days.note: Being the instrument still means you choose and answer for what you do.

days.heading: Four hundred thin cows

story.title: Satyakama Jabala
story.body: Young Satyakama wanted to study, but he didn't know his father's lineage. He told the teacher exactly what his mother had told him. The teacher accepted him for that honesty and handed him four hundred weak, thin cows to look after. Satyakama said he wouldn't come back until they were a thousand. He spent years in the forest, and returned with a thousand cows and a mind that nature itself had taught.
story.lesson: Start honestly, start small, and stay with it.

verse.sanskrit: ता अभिप्रस्थापयन्नुवाच नासहस्रेणावर्तेयेति स ह वर्षगणं प्रोवास ता यदा सहस्रꣳ सम्पेदुः ॥
verse.line: Given four hundred weak cows, he said, 'I won't come back until they are a thousand.' He stayed years.

days.forYou: Satyakama began with very little: no lineage, thin cows and a long road. Your start may look small too. What he did next is what counted.
days.today: Set your own 'thousand cows' goal for this new chapter, and write it down.

faq.q: Which Bhagavad Gita verse is good for a new beginning?
faq.a: 6.3 says that for someone starting out, action is the way. 18.48 reminds you that every new undertaking has flaws, like fire has smoke, and 4.42 asks you to cut doubt and stand up.

faq.q: What does the Gita say about starting a new job?
faq.a: Keep doing the work well without clinging to results (3.19), don't drop work that suits you because it has flaws (18.48), and play your part in the larger whole (11.33).

faq.q: Is there a Gita verse for courage to start?
faq.a: 4.42 ends with uttiṣṭha: cut the doubt in your heart and stand up. 11.33 opens the same way: rise and do your part.
